title: Solving GraphQL N+1 Queries with DataLoader
prompt: A mobile app release adds a `seller { rating }` field to the Order History screen, issuing `orders(first: 50) { id items { qty product { id title seller { id name rating } } } }`. Your Apollo/Java GraphQL Gateway resolves each field independently: 1 query for 50 orders -> 50 queries for items -> 200 queries for products -> 200 gRPC calls for sellers = **451 backend calls per HTTP request**. At just 60 mobile RPS, backend traffic surges to **27,060 QPS**, saturating PostgreSQL and `Seller-Service` and causing 503s. Redesign the GraphQL execution layer to bound backend queries and protect against arbitrary nested queries.

learningJourney.title: Enterprise solution: Request-Scoped DataLoader + Complexity Limits

explanation.foundation: Reduce 451 calls to `<= 4` batched calls while blocking abusive queries:
explanation.core:
- **Request-Scoped `DataLoader` per Tier**: Instantiate `OrderItemsLoader`, `ProductLoader`, and `SellerDataLoader` per HTTP request so in-request deduplication never bleeds across users. Use `WHERE id = ANY($1)` (Postgres) and `BatchGetSellers(ids)` (gRPC) with `maxBatchSize=500`.
- **Query Complexity & Depth Limits**: Reject queries with depth `> 6` or complexity score `> 1,000` (where list arguments like `first: 50` multiply child cost) *before* execution.
- **Persisted Query Allowlists (APQ)**: In production, accept only SHA-256 registered query hashes from mobile clients.
